canonical_protocol: Full 3,900-image CelebA-Spoof test set; deployment-style face crops (BlazeFace detection + 25% margin, falling back to the dataset's own official bounding box when BlazeFace misses -- see build_face_cropped_dataset.py); plain 0.5 decision threshold. n=3900 for every model under this protocol (fallback crops mean no image is ever excluded).
blazeface_only_protocol: Same 3,900-image test set, but using ONLY live BlazeFace detection -- no bbox fallback. Images where BlazeFace finds no face get NO decision at all (matching true live-webcam behavior, where no official bounding box exists to fall back to). n < 3900; see 'n' and 'coverage' fields for the exact count.

consistency_notes.numbers: v1 deployment-crop accuracy reported as both 95.94% (TASK F) and 94.54% (TASK G v1-vs-v2 table)
consistency_notes.explanation: 95.94% used BLAZEFACE_ONLY_PROTOCOL (n=3839/3900 -- the 61 images where live BlazeFace detection missed were excluded entirely, matching true deployment behavior where there is no fallback). 94.54% used CANONICAL_PROTOCOL (n=3900 -- those same 61 images got a crop via the dataset's own official bounding box, which only exists for this labeled benchmark, not for a live webcam frame). Both are real numbers computed correctly; they simply answer different questions. 94.54% is the one reported under 'v1_vs_v2' below (canonical).

consistency_notes.numbers: v2 accuracy reported as both 99.04% (masked-eval's unmasked baseline) and 98.69% (TASK G headline)
consistency_notes.explanation: Same root cause as above. 99.04% is BLAZEFACE_ONLY_PROTOCOL (n=3839), deliberately chosen as the masked-eval baseline because bbox fallback isn't a fair stand-in for a MASKED face -- the dataset's official bounding box was computed on the unmasked face, so using it when a mask causes a miss would hide exactly the Stage-1 effect masked-eval exists to measure. 98.69% is CANONICAL_PROTOCOL (n=3900) and is the number reported under 'headline' and 'backbone_comparison' below. The masked-eval section is intentionally NOT on the canonical protocol and is labeled as such.

mobilenet_v3_small.note: Illumination/environment breakdowns are computed over spoof images only (live images carry no real illumination/environment code in this dataset's own annotations -- verified directly on the raw label data). Only APCER is reported for those two breakdowns, not BPCER/accuracy, since there is no live subgroup within a single illumination/environment bucket to compute them against.

gray_zone.protocol: Band selected on the VALIDATION set only (never test); applied to the canonical-protocol test set (n=3900). v2 (mobilenet_v3_small) only.
gray_zone.band_selected_on: validation set only (predictions_val.csv) -- test set never used for band selection

masked_eval.protocol: RAW test images (live+spoof) with a synthetic surgical-mask overlay (nose-to-chin, white/light_blue/black), then BLAZEFACE-ONLY detection (no bbox fallback -- see consistency_notes). The unmasked baseline here uses the SAME BlazeFace-only methodology for a fair comparison, and is NOT the canonical headline number.
masked_eval.unmasked_baseline_protocol: Same 3,900-image test set, but using ONLY live BlazeFace detection -- no bbox fallback. Images where BlazeFace finds no face get NO decision at all (matching true live-webcam behavior, where no official bounding box exists to fall back to). n < 3900; see 'n' and 'coverage' fields for the exact count.
